phase: 4/4 - settlement + reconcile + bench + report (all must-have v1 complete, measured)
machine: Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 24 GB RAM, macOS 25.4.0 (Darwin, arm64)
stack: Go 1.26.3 (module baseline go 1.25), PostgreSQL 16.14 (native Homebrew, localhost:5432) via pgx v5, net/http (Go 1.22 method routing), go test -race, goroutine load harness. docker-compose.yml provided (Docker daemon was not running; native pg used per spec fallback).
database: native Homebrew PostgreSQL 16.14; databases ledgercore + ledgercore_test; trust auth; row-lock (READ COMMITTED + SELECT FOR UPDATE) default, SERIALIZABLE mode available
tests: 35 passed / 0 failed; go test -race clean (0 data races); coverage ledger 92.3% money 89.7% settle 78.8% ops 71.6% store 45.4% api 50.0%

measurement_methodology.money_conservation: monitor goroutine runs SUM(balance) GROUP BY currency (single consistent MVCC snapshot) 17213x DURING the 96000-transfer storm; every sample nets to 0 per currency and every shared-account MIN(balance) >= 0. Independently re-verified by the reconciliation job recomputing balances from the journal (SUM of postings) == cached balances, zero drift.
measurement_methodology.double_spend_lost_update: no-negative constraint checked on new balances while holding SELECT FOR UPDATE locks on all involved accounts (deterministic ascending-id lock order avoids deadlock); adversarial 64-worker/4-account/$50 drain fired the constraint 31158 times with 0 negatives, 0 lost updates. Final Σ(shared balances) == seeded total => no lost updates.
measurement_methodology.idempotency: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING RETURNING inside the same transaction as the posting; a concurrent duplicate blocks on the in-flight insert until the owner commits/aborts, so exactly one posts and retries return the stored response. 16000 concurrent duplicate submissions across 500 keys -> 0 duplicate postings.
measurement_methodology.fx: cross-currency move posts 4 balanced legs (2 per currency) through per-currency FX position accounts; toAmount = round(fromAmount * num/den) via exact big.Int rational math (no floats); each currency nets to 0.
measurement_methodology.reconciliation: settle.Reconcile asserts (a) every txn balances per currency, (b) derived==stored per account, (c) net==0 per currency; TestReconcileDetectsInjectedDrift proves it is non-vacuous (a +1 minor-unit corruption is flagged).
measurement_methodology.throughput_latency: go loadgen: 32 goroutines x 3000 transfers on 32 shared accounts, pgxpool sized to workers+4, native localhost Postgres (no network hop); per-op wall-clock durations, nearest-rank percentiles. Machine-dependent.

notes: All Must-have v1 delivered: immutable double-entry journal (balanced legs, debits==credits per currency), integer minor-units money (no floats), derived balances, transfer/payment/refund + multi-currency FX, idempotency keys (exactly-once), row-locked concurrency safety (no double-spend/lost-update/disallowed-negative), settlement batch (per-merchant netting w/ refunds -> payout) + reconciliation (zero drift), HTTP API (JSON envelope, Idempotency-Key), and a seeded Go concurrent load harness writing results/*.json. Should-have included: SERIALIZABLE-vs-row-lock comparison. Out of scope (not built): hold/capture auth, hash-chained audit log, outbox events, real PSP/bank rails, UI, sharding. KEY DECISION: native Postgres (Docker daemon not running); DATABASE_URL/TEST_DATABASE_URL configurable, docker-compose.yml provided as equivalent. CODE REVIEW: a background go-reviewer found ONE CRITICAL settlement double-pay race (net computed before merchant/payout row locks were held) — FIXED (RunSettlement now locks merchant+payout FOR UPDATE and computes net under locks) + regression test TestConcurrentSettlementPaysExactlyOnce (16 concurrent runs -> paid once); idempotency/posting-locks/refund-bound/FX math reviewed sound.
